questions.stem: 45-year-old woman presents with fluctuating muscle weakness that worsens with repetitive activity and improves with rest. She also reports more pronounced symptoms in the evening. Neurological examination shows normal deep tendon reflexes. Workup reveals positive anti-MuSK antibodies and negative anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibodies. Which of the following best describes the underlying mechanism of her condition?

options.label: A
options.text: T-cell mediated destruction of anterior horn cells

options.label: B
options.text: Autoantibodies disrupt clustering of acetylcholine receptors

options.label: C
options.text: Disruption of post synaptic voltage-gated calcium channels

options.label: D
options.text: Inhibition of acetylcholine release from synaptic vesicles
